title: General Agents Contain World Models, even under Partial Observability and Stochasticity
claim: Extends Richens et al. 2025 to stochastic agents and partially observable environments; less powerful agents also contain world models.
relevance: World-model selection theorem line; no self-models.

title: What Capable Agents Must Know: Selection Theorems for Robust Decision-Making under Uncertainty
claim: Low average-case regret forces world models, belief-like memory under partial observability, informational modularity under block-structured tests (Cor. 3) and regime-tracking memory under shifting task mixtures (Cor. 4).
relevance: Closest competitor to the SM self-model theorem: if self-shift vs world-shift are treated as regimes, Cor. 4 may already imply part of SM. Regime here is an index of the evaluation protocol; no self-models discussed.
verified: web-2026-10-08 partial full text (HTML v2, first 100k chars: Cor. 3-4, discussion)

authors: Ranjan, Saurabh and Sokratous, Konstantina and Odegaard, Brian
title: Reality Monitoring in Large Language Models: Self-Knowledge That Transforms with Conversation Memory
claim: LLMs can identify self-generated vs user-provided items when memory demands are low; advantage disappears with delays; confidence-accuracy links break in some models.
relevance: Source/reality monitoring precedent (P7).

authors: Wang, Andy and Mahajan, Parv and Africa, David Demitri and Souly, Alexandra and Taylor, Jordan and Kirk, Robert
title: Prefill Awareness in Large Language Models
claim: Frontier models detect inserted assistant turns opposing their preferences (e.g., 9-35% at 0% FPR); detection driven by stylistic mismatch, reversion by preference mismatch.
relevance: Shows authorship/agency program (P7) is already well covered.

authors: Richens, Jonathan and Everitt, Tom and Abel, David
title: General agents need world models
details: arXiv versions later retitled 'General agents contain world models'.
claim: A goal-conditioned policy with success >= (1-delta) x optimal on depth-n composite goals in a finite, communicating, stationary controlled Markov process determines a transition estimate with error O(delta/sqrt(n)) + O(1/n).
relevance: World-model necessity for multi-step agents; stationary environment and fixed agent, so no self-model or changing-agent case.
verified: web-2026-10-08 partial full text (HTML v5 Theorem 1; authors from PMLR page)

authors: Virgo, Nathaniel and Biehl, Martin and Baltieri, Manuel and Capucci, Matteo
title: A "good regulator theorem" for embodied agents
claim: Every good regulator can be read by an observer as having (possibly trivial) possibilistic beliefs about its environment; models are observer-relative.
relevance: Red-team source: selection theorems license observer-relative models, not internal representations.

title: Inspection and Control of Self-Generated-Text Recognition Ability in Llama3-8b-Instruct
claim: A residual-stream direction underlies self-authorship recognition and can be steered.
relevance: P7 precedent.

title: Robust agents learn causal world models
claim: Policies with delta-bounded regret under all local interventions (and mixtures) identify an approximate causal model of the environment (Thm 1-2); a causal model suffices for low-regret policies (Thm 3).
relevance: Template for a self-model selection theorem; the agent's decision is kept outside the modelled variables, so self-models are not covered.
limitations: Unmediated decision tasks only; agent is told the shift; causal sufficiency; fixed utility.
verified: web-2026-10-08 partial full text (HTML v7, first 100k chars: setup, theorems, assumptions, limitations)

title: Some Existing Selection Theorems
details: Posted 30 Sep 2021; the self-modelling exchange is in the comments (question by Davey Morse; reply by the author).
claim: Survey of existing selection theorems. In the comments, asked whether any selection theorem predicts when an agent models a self distinct from its environment, the author replies 'None that I know of; it's a topic ripe for exploration.'
relevance: Evidence that self-model selection theorems were recognised as open.
verified: web-2026-10-08 (post page and comments, summarised fetch)

title: A Brain-like Synergistic Core in LLMs Drives Behaviour and Learning
claim: Information-decomposition analysis finds a synergistic core in LLMs relevant to behaviour and learning.
relevance: Integration measures in LLMs (descriptive complement).

title: A theoretically based index of consciousness independent of sensory processing and behavior
claim: Perturbational Complexity Index discriminates conscious vs unconscious states.
relevance: Possible descriptive measure; Phua (2025) shows counterintuitive behaviour in agents.

title: Principles for Responsible AI Consciousness Research
claim: Five principles for responsible research that might create conscious AI; organisations should publicly commit.
relevance: Ethics protocol for this project.

authors: Long, Robert and Sebo, Jeff and Butlin, Patrick and Finlinson, Kathleen and Fish, Kyle and Harding, Jacqueline and Pfau, Jacob and Sims, Toni and Birch, Jonathan and Chalmers, David
title: Taking AI Welfare Seriously
claim: Realistic possibility of AI consciousness/agency in near future warrants welfare preparation.
relevance: Ethics context.

title: Artificial Suffering: An Argument for a Global Moratorium on Synthetic Phenomenology
venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Consciousness
claim: Risk of creating artificial suffering justifies moratorium on synthetic phenomenology research.
relevance: Why valence/affect programs are excluded.

authors: Butlin, Patrick and Long, Robert and Bayne, Tim and others
title: Identifying indicators of consciousness in AI systems
claim: Theory-derived indicator properties (RPT, GWT, HOT, PP, AST, agency) used to assess AI systems.
relevance: Indicator framework treats workspace and metacognition as separate indicators.
limitations: Author list partially from search result.

title: Illusions of AI consciousness
claim: Beliefs in AI consciousness will likely grow as AI improves; projecting moral status and self-preservation goals onto AI carries risks.
relevance: Ethical framing; supports not over-claiming.

authors: Butlin, Patrick and Long, Robert and Bayne, Tim and Bengio, Yoshua and Birch, Jonathan and Chalmers, David and Constant, Axel and Deane, George and Elmoznino, Eric and Fleming, Stephen M. and Ji, Xu and Kanai, Ryota and Klein, Colin and Lindsay, Grace and Michel, Matthias and Mudrik, Liad and Peters, Megan A. K. and Schwitzgebel, Eric and Simon, Jonathan and VanRullen, Rufin
title: Identifying indicators of consciousness in AI systems
claim: Derive indicator properties from neuroscientific theories (assuming computational functionalism as a working hypothesis) and use them to assess AI systems; both over- and under-attribution are risks.
relevance: Canonical framework our Level-2 claims must map onto; defines indicators (GWT, RPT, HOT, AST, PP, agency/embodiment).
limitations: Indicators assessed largely by architectural inspection rather than measurement; theory-heavy; inherits uncertainty of each theory.

title: The Edge of Sentience: Risk and Precaution in Humans, Other Animals, and AI
claim: Precautionary framework; for AI, behavioural markers face the 'gaming problem' because systems trained on human data can mimic markers.
relevance: The gaming problem is the core methodological threat our designs address.

title: Simulacra as Conscious Exotica
claim: LLM-based role-play simulacra are 'conscious exotica'; consciousness talk may not apply in ordinary ways.
relevance: Reminds us self-reports belong to role-played characters, not necessarily the system.

authors: Butlin, Patrick and Long, Robert and Elmoznino, Eric and Bengio, Yoshua and others
title: Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness
claim: Long report deriving 14 indicator properties from GWT, RPT, HOT, AST, PP and agency/embodiment; concludes no current system is a strong candidate but no obvious technical barriers.
relevance: Detailed indicator list (e.g., GWT-1..4, HOT-1..4, AST-1) used to label our measured properties.
limitations: Same as TiCS version; LLM assessment done by architecture description.

title: Could a Large Language Model be Conscious?
claim: Mainstream assumptions identify obstacles in current LLMs (no recurrent processing, no global workspace, no unified agency) that may be overcome within a decade.
relevance: Frames recurrence/workspace/agency as candidate engineering pathways; widely cited baseline position.
limitations: Philosophical assessment; predates mechanistic evidence such as J-space.

title: Unlimited Associative Learning as a Null Hypothesis
claim: Standard causal-reasoning tasks can be explained by a powerful form of associative learning (UAL); urges broader hypothesis spaces.
relevance: Related critique of UAL as a marker.

authors: Birch, Jonathan and Ginsburg, Simona and Jablonka, Eva
title: Unlimited Associative Learning and the origins of consciousness: a primer and some predictions
claim: UAL (compound and novel stimuli, second-order and trace conditioning, rewritable values) proposed as a transition marker of minimal consciousness; engineered systems with UAL-like learning but no hallmarks are declared 'derivative'.
relevance: Eliminates the UAL minimal-machine candidate: the predictable positive result is pre-empted.

title: Open-Weight Masked Introspection: Measuring What Language Models Can Report About Their Own Computation
claim: Across 8 open models and >78k measurements, verbal reports do not discriminate real interventions from sham/impact-matched perturbations (AUROC ~0.50), while linear probes recover intervention presence at 75-96%.
relevance: Strong negative result; information present internally but not routed to report -- 'access without report' framing; informs our use of sham/impact-matched controls.
limitations: Single author; preprint; conflicts with positive replications (needs reconciliation).

authors: Guo, Zifan Carl and Ruis, Laura and Andreas, Jacob and Li, Belinda Z.
title: Introspective Coupling: Self-Explanation Training Tracks Behavioral Change Despite Fixed Supervision
claim: Explanations trained on fixed (outdated) targets come to track the model's current behaviour when explanation training co-occurs with other post-training.
relevance: Close to P1/P6 'tracking change' theme; behaviour-level rather than lesion-level.

title: Emergent Introspection in AI is Content-Agnostic
claim: In large open models, injection detection occurs without reliable content identification; confabulated contents are high-frequency concrete concepts.
relevance: Supports 'generic anomaly signal' interpretation; our lesion design must separate generic anomaly from content-specific self-tracking (sham lesions).

authors: Macar, Uzay and Yang, Li and Wang, Atticus and Wallich, Peter and Ameisen, Emmanuel and Lindsey, Jack
title: Mechanisms of Introspective Awareness
claim: Injection detection emerges from post-training (DPO, not SFT); two-stage circuit: early 'evidence carrier' features suppress late 'gate' features that produce default 'no'; identification largely separate from detection; refusal ablation and trained bias vectors raise detection.
relevance: Mechanistic precedent for dissociable detection vs content circuits; shows post-training shapes self-report pathways (confound for any self-report work).
limitations: Specific to injection paradigm; open models studied per abstract only (full text not yet read).

title: Mechanisms of Introspective Awareness
claim: Gemma3-27B, Qwen3-235B, OLMo-3.1-32B: injected-concept detection via a distributed anomaly-detection circuit (evidence carriers suppress a 'say No' gate); detection and identification use separate mechanisms.
relevance: Injection-detection mechanisms; not metacognition about own knowledge.

title: Me, Myself, and pi: Evaluating and Explaining LLM Introspection
claim: Policy-introspection taxonomy; self vs other-model introspection accuracy as identification strategy; mechanistic 'attention diffusion' account.
relevance: D1: self-vs-other cross-model identification logic (as in Binder et al.).
limitations: No input-fixed competence intervention or within-target estimand.

authors: Pearson-Vogel, Theia and Vanek, Martin and Douglas, Raymond and Kulveit, Jan
title: Latent Introspection: Models Can Detect Prior Concept Injections
claim: Qwen 32B shows latent (logit-lens) detection signals of prior injections in mid layers that are suppressed before output; prompting raises sensitivity from 0.3% to ~40%.
relevance: Internal signals can exist without report (relevant to report vs access dissociations).

authors: Singh, Shashwat and Linzen, Tal and Ravfogel, Shauli
title: Can LLMs Introspect? A Reality Check
claim: Two necessary conditions: privileged access (not solvable from input cues) and second-order computation. Input-only probes match Ji-An et al. and belief-dominance results; models cannot distinguish activation steering from input-level 'gaslight' manipulation.
relevance: Closest methodological ally/competitor; explicitly calls for designs where first- and second-order accounts diverge plus mechanistic evidence -- exactly what P1 lesion design targets.
limitations: Does not use lesions/ablations of competence; focuses on re-analysis of existing paradigms.

authors: Berg, Cameron and de Lucena, Diogo Schwerz and Rosenblatt, Judd
title: Large Language Models Report Subjective Experience Under Self-Referential Processing
claim: Self-referential prompting reliably elicits first-person experience reports across model families; reports increase when deception-related SAE features are suppressed.
relevance: Example of self-report-centred evidence we deliberately do not rely on.

authors: Binder, Felix J. and Chua, James and Korbak, Tomek and Sleight, Henry and Hughes, John and Long, Robert and Perez, Ethan and Turpin, Miles and Evans, Owain
title: Looking Inward: Language Models Can Learn About Themselves by Introspection
claim: Models fine-tuned to predict their own hypothetical behaviour predict themselves better than other models trained on their behaviour; self-prediction tracks deliberate behaviour changes after further fine-tuning.
relevance: Precedent for self-vs-cross-prediction control and for 'tracking change'; P1 extends to item-specific mechanistic lesions with input fixed.
limitations: Simple tasks; requires fine-tuning; failure on complex tasks.

authors: Comsa, Iulia M. and Shanahan, Murray
title: Does It Make Sense to Speak of Introspection in Large Language Models?
claim: Introspection attributions require a causal connection between internal states and the self-report; some LLM self-reports (e.g., about temperature) can qualify minimally, others (creative-process reports) do not.
relevance: Conceptual grounding for the causal criterion.

authors: Hahami, Ely and Sinha, Ishaan and Jain, Lavik and Kaplan, Josh and Hahami, Jon
title: Detecting the Disturbance: A Nuanced View of Introspective Abilities in LLMs
claim: In Llama-3.1-8B, apparent injection detection is explained by global logit shifts toward 'yes'; but localisation (which of 10 sentences) and strength discrimination are above chance for early-layer injections.
relevance: Key confound (response-bias shifts) our P1 readouts must control (use symmetric/forced-choice and bias-corrected type-2 measures).

title: Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models
claim: Concept injection: Claude Opus 4/4.1 sometimes detect and name injected concepts (~20% with ~0 false positives); defines criteria accuracy, grounding, internality, metacognitive representation.
relevance: Source of the causal-grounding criterion we generalise to competence lesions; paradigm now heavily replicated/critiqued.
limitations: Unreliable, context-dependent; mostly proprietary models; detection may reflect anomaly detection or logit shifts.

authors: Plunkett, Dillon and Morris, Adam and Reddy, Keerthi and Morales, Jorge
title: Self-Interpretability: LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that Drive Their Decisions, and Improve with Training
claim: Models fine-tuned to have quantitative preferences can report them; training to report generalises to native preferences.
relevance: Evidence that self-report training can generalise beyond training targets (relevant to P1 developmental extension and P5).
limitations: Reports about behavioural weights, not mechanistic states.

authors: Song, Siyuan and Hu, Jennifer and Mahowald, Kyle
title: Language Models Fail to Introspect About Their Knowledge of Language
claim: Metalinguistic prompts and internal probabilities agree no better within a model than across similar models: no evidence of privileged self-access for grammatical knowledge.
relevance: Negative baseline; self-vs-other comparison methodology.

authors: Song, Siyuan and Lederman, Harvey and Hu, Jennifer and Mahowald, Kyle
title: Privileged Self-Access Matters for Introspection in AI
claim: Defines introspection as yielding information about internal states more reliably than any equal-or-cheaper third-party process; models are not better at predicting their own sampling temperature than other models are.
relevance: Operational definition of privileged access we adopt as a necessary (not sufficient) criterion.

title: What forms could introspective systems take? A research programme
claim: Framework for diverse possible introspective architectures beyond the human case.
relevance: Conceptual space for non-human-like self-monitoring.

title: Towards Evaluating AI Systems for Moral Status Using Self-Reports
claim: Proposes training models to answer verifiable questions about themselves to make self-reports about morally relevant states more reliable.
relevance: P1 provides a validity test for such self-report training (does it generalise to untrained internal changes?).

authors: Turpin, Miles and Michael, Julian and Perez, Ethan and Bowman, Samuel R.
title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
claim: CoT explanations can systematically misrepresent the real reasons for predictions.
relevance: Verbal self-explanation is not evidence of access.

title: On Emergent Capabilities and Model Merging
claim: LoRA merges of single-task parents cannot reach a superadditive capability of a jointly trained oracle (taboo extraction 23.7% vs <9.5%); the capability lies largely outside the parents' span.
relevance: Closest precedent for 'integration produces superadditive capability' (not consciousness-related; weight merging only).

authors: Akiba, Takuya and Shing, Makoto and Tang, Yujin
title: Evolutionary optimization of model merging recipes
details: 7:195-204; arXiv id entered from memory - verify
claim: Evolutionary search over merges yields models with cross-domain capability combinations (e.g., Japanese math) without additional training.
relevance: Merging can compose capabilities -- but compositional skill, not consciousness-specific.

title: LoRA Soups: Merging LoRAs for Practical Skill Composition Tasks
claim: Learnable concatenation of skill-specific LoRAs outperforms data mixing on binary skill composition.
relevance: Direct test-bed for the researcher's adapter-integration seed (Pilot C).

authors: Ilharco, Gabriel and Ribeiro, Marco Tulio and Wortsman, Mitchell and Gururangan, Suchin and Schmidt, Ludwig and Hajishirzi, Hannaneh and Farhadi, Ali
title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
claim: Task vectors can be added/negated to compose or remove capabilities.
relevance: Merging mechanism for Pilot C.

authors: Okawa, Maya and Lubana, Ekdeep Singh and Dick, Robert P. and Tanaka, Hidenori
title: Compositional Abilities Emerge Multiplicatively: Exploring Diffusion Models on a Synthetic Task
claim: Compositional abilities appear abruptly because they depend multiplicatively on component capabilities.
relevance: Null model for 'superadditivity': multiplicative composition yields apparent emergence without new mechanism.

authors: Yadav, Prateek and Tam, Derek and Choshen, Leshem and Raffel, Colin and Bansal, Mohit
title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
claim: Trim/elect-sign/merge reduces interference among task vectors.
relevance: Merging baseline for Pilot C.

title: Evidence for Limited Metacognition in LLMs
claim: Animal-cognition-inspired paradigms (strategic use of confidence, e.g., opt-out) show limited, context-dependent metacognition in frontier LLMs, growing since 2024 and shaped by post-training.
relevance: Behavioural metacognition paradigms without self-report; candidate DVs (opt-out) for P1/P5.
limitations: Behavioural; cannot separate self- vs world-tracking.

authors: Aoki, Koshiro and Takatsuki, Ryota and Minegishi, Gouki and Haruki, Yusuke and Kawahara, Daisuke
title: In-Context Neurofeedback: Can LLMs Control Their Internal Representations through Privileged Access?
claim: When neurofeedback targets are made genuinely privileged (not inferable from prompts), models do not show reliable control.
relevance: Reinforces privileged-access requirement.

title: Closing the Confidence-Faithfulness Gap in Large Language Models
claim: Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B (base and instruct): calibration (accuracy) and verbalised-confidence directions are linear and nearly orthogonal; CAA steering shifts verbal confidence; joint solving inverts alignment.
relevance: Confidence subspaces exist; no workspace link.

authors: Cohen, Roi and de Melo, Gerard
title: The Source of Competence Shapes Metacognition in Language Models
details: OpenReview id h4y6IIKNzV; not found on arXiv (author arXiv listing checked 2026-10-01)
claim: Six 'source of competence' regimes: strong parametric memory; evidence-grounded (RAG); deliberative reasoning (CoT); partial/stale memory (rare or outdated facts, e.g. CEO changes); heuristic pattern matching (shortcuts / reduced-model approximations); computation-degraded (4/8-bit quantisation or noise injection into internal states). Datasets partitioned by prominence (TriviaQA, NQ, LAMA-style, GSM8K, StrategyQA, CSQA, SQuAD). Confidence channels: verbalised, token log-prob, self-consistency. Matched-accuracy divergence (~61% acc: partial memory +27 pt gap vs evidence-grounded +5 pt); stale facts +33 pt; 'danger zone' where accuracy falls sharply while confidence stays high.
relevance: CLOSEST COMPETITOR. Establishes that globally degrading competence, or selecting low-competence item regimes, leaves confidence high. Per available reconstruction it does NOT use item-specific input-preserving lesions, sham/unrelated/input-corruption controls, or internal-representation analyses ('behavioral rather than internal metacognition').
limitations: Full text blocked by OpenReview Cloudflare check; reconstruction from Lacuna summary + search snippets (secondary). MUST be confirmed from the PDF.

title: Continual Calibration: Coverage Can Collapse Before Accuracy in Lifelong LLM Fine-Tuning
claim: Under sequential fine-tuning, conformal coverage and calibration degrade faster than accuracy (aggregate, per task); driven by score-distribution drift.
relevance: D1/D2: confidence under self-generated capability change, but aggregate only; no item-level within-target tracking or pre-change adjustment.

title: Recognition-Refusal Misalignment in LLMs: Why Models Answer Structurally Unanswerable Questions
claim: Models linearly encode 'no admissible answer' but this direction is nearly orthogonal to refusal; steering it changes abstention (1.7B-70B).
relevance: Monitoring signal exists but is not routed to control -- 'routing not encoding' failure analogous to anosognosia/anosodiaphoria.

title: Evidence Integration in Large Language Models
claim: Twelve LLMs; models accept invalid external candidates 93-100% despite internal verification; verification states decodable but little-to-no causal impact on answers; J-lens decomposition shows verification dissociable from integration.
relevance: Monitoring-control dissociation with J-lens; neighbour of the control-routing candidate.
limitations: Summarised from PDF via fetch tool.

authors: Kumaran, Dharshan and Daw, Nathaniel and Osindero, Simon and Veli{\v{c}}kovi{\'c}, Petar and Patraucean, Viorica
title: Causal evidence that language models use confidence to drive behaviour
claim: Activation steering of an internal confidence signal shifts abstention; models apply thresholds to internal confidence; verbal confidence independently predicts abstention.
relevance: D1: causal test of confidence USE (steering the confidence representation), not of whether confidence tracks an input-fixed competence change.
limitations: Intervenes on the confidence representation, not on competence.

title: Decomposing and Steering Functional Metacognition in Large Language Models
claim: Linear probes find six functional metacognitive directions (incl. self-assessed capability, computational effort); steering them causally changes reasoning behaviour.
relevance: Prior art for 'internal metacognitive variables causally drive control'; not tested against interventions on competence.

authors: Liu, Gabrielle Kaili-May and Gani, Areeb and Lu, Jacqueline and Thomas, Jordan and Steyvers, Mark and Cohan, Arman
title: Metacognition in LLMs: Foundations, Progress, and Opportunities
claim: Survey of LLM metacognition (monitoring, control, measurement).
relevance: Use for systematic novelty check of P1 before committing.
limitations: Survey; not yet read in full.

title: Predictive metacognition: a neuro-computational framework for self-monitoring in large language models
claim: LoRA fine-tuning with a metacognitive loss improves calibration (Brier/ECE) in Llama-3-8B and Phi-3-mini.
relevance: Example of trained self-monitoring evaluated only by aggregate calibration -- no lesion or privileged-access tests (the gap P1 fills).

title: MetaErr: Towards Predicting Error Patterns in Deep Neural Networks
claim: Predicting error patterns of DNNs (meta-model lineage).
relevance: Meta-model lineage.

title: LLMs Show No Signs Of Individuated Metacognition
claim: Across 20 frontier LLMs and 6 benchmarks, cross-model confidence is approximately rank-one (shared item difficulty); pairwise calibration vanishes after controlling for shared difficulty.
relevance: Strong motivation for P1's world-tracking hypothesis: confidence may encode a generic difficulty model rather than self-specific competence.
limitations: Verbalised confidence; between-model design (cannot isolate within-model causal dependence).

title: How LLMs Detect and Correct Their Own Errors: The Role of Internal Confidence Signals
claim: Gemma 3 27B, Qwen 2.5 7B: a post-answer-newline (PANL) confidence representation is causally sufficient (patching restores ~74%) but not necessary (redundant with other positions) for error detection; predicts correction success.
relevance: Causal error-monitoring neighbour; no workspace link; no factorial.

authors: Park, Sangjun and Meyerson, Elliot and Qiu, Xin and Miikkulainen, Risto
title: Fine-Tuning Language Models to Know What They Know
claim: Evolution-strategy metacognitive alignment improves type-2 d' and generalises to unseen datasets, languages and newly acquired knowledge; driven by sparse parameters.
relevance: Trained metacognition that generalises to 'newly acquired knowledge' -- relevant comparator for P1 developmental arm (we test generalisation to removed knowledge).

title: Operational Proto-Introspection in Looped Language Models: Process-Quality Taps, Executable Branching, and the Readout-Control Boundary
claim: Frozen Ouro-RLTT (2.6B, 4 loops): hidden states predict success beyond shortcuts, but no frozen intervention converts the readable signal into control ('the direction that predicts success is not a direction that, written back, produces success').
relevance: Readout-control boundary; neighbour of the monitoring x control candidate.

title: From Signals to Transfer: A Factorised Study of Probe-Based Uncertainty Estimation in Large Language Models
claim: Factorised study of probe-based hallucination/uncertainty detection (features, training data, evaluation shift); search snippets report Procrustes-aligned cross-model probe transfer approaching target-native AUROC.
relevance: Prior evidence for generic (alignable) competence/uncertainty decoding across models -- informs Stage-1 S-family predictions.
limitations: Transfer numbers come from a search snippet, not the abstract; verify.

authors: Steyvers, Mark and Peters, Megan A. K.
title: Metacognition and Uncertainty Communication in Humans and Large Language Models
claim: Compares human and LLM metacognition and uncertainty communication; calls for psychological measurement standards.
relevance: Measurement framing (type-2 sensitivity vs bias).

title: TRAPSBench: Vision-Language Models Encode but Fail to Express Epistemic Restraint
claim: VLMs encode an answerable/unanswerable distinction; injecting the signal at one layer induces abstention.
relevance: F => C via steering in VLMs (not route-specific).

title: The Hidden Signal of Verifier Strictness: Controlling and Improving Step-Wise Verification via Selective Latent Steering
claim: Steering a latent correctness signal near verification-paragraph boundaries changes a generative verifier's accept/reject verdicts (sample-level 'selective' routing of the intervention).
relevance: Generic sufficiency at the level of verification REPORTS; not use/control of a candidate, not workspace-route-specific.

authors: Yax, Nicolas and Palminteri, Stefano and Oudeyer, Pierre-Yves
title: LLMs learn different forms of metacognition when trained to predict their own accuracy
claim: Fine-tuning 10 open LLMs to predict own accuracy yields two signals: output-consistency tracking (early, generalises across datasets) and accuracy tracking (later, local to training distribution).
relevance: Directly relevant to P5*: trained monitors may learn a readout of answer-distribution concentration rather than self-tracking; lesion tests discriminate the two.
limitations: Very recent (2026-09-27); full text not read.

authors: Zhang, Hefan and Zhang, Bingquan and Cheng, Ming and Hassanpour, Saeed and Ma, Weicheng and Vosoughi, Soroush
title: When Linguistic and Internal Confidence Diverge in Large Language Models
claim: Across 30 models, verbal confidence weakly associates with logit-based confidence at instance level; instruction tuning inflates confidence.
relevance: Need multiple confidence readouts in P1; verbal readouts alone are unreliable.

authors: Zhao, Tianyi and He, Yinhan and Zheng, Wendy and Zhang, Yujie and Chen, Chen
title: Wired for Overconfidence: A Mechanistic Perspective on Inflated Verbalized Confidence in LLMs
claim: Compact mid-late-layer circuits causally inflate verbalised confidence, especially on wrong answers; ablation/steering recalibrates.
relevance: Mechanistic account of the verbal-confidence channel (one reason verbal confidence is a poor E3 endpoint).

authors: Li, Ji-An and Xiong, Huadong and Wilson, Robert C. and Mattar, Marcelo G. and Benna, Marcus K.
title: Language Models Are Capable of Metacognitive Monitoring and Control of Their Internal Activations
claim: Neurofeedback paradigm: LLMs learn in context to report and control projections of their activations onto directions, better for semantically interpretable directions.
relevance: Prior 'metacognitive space' claim; later critiqued (Singh 2026; Aoki 2026) as solvable from input-level information.

title: LLM-Independent Adaptive RAG: Let the Question Speak for Itself
claim: Question-only features (27 features, no LLM access) match LLM-uncertainty methods for deciding when to retrieve.
relevance: KEY EVIDENCE that on natural data, world/difficulty-tracking is observationally sufficient -- motivates interventional identification.

authors: Moskvoretskii, Viktor and Lysyuk, Maria and Salnikov, Mikhail and others
title: Adaptive Retrieval Without Self-Knowledge? Bringing Uncertainty Back Home
claim: 35 adaptive-retrieval/uncertainty methods: many adaptive retrieval methods show near-zero self-knowledge; simple uncertainty estimators do as well.
relevance: Retrieval/tool-request as a metacognitive control endpoint has been evaluated observationally -- not under competence lesions (as far as found).

title: Calibrating Verbal Uncertainty as a Linear Feature to Reduce Hallucinations
claim: Steering a verbal-uncertainty feature in line with internal (semantic) uncertainty reduces hallucination.
relevance: Sufficiency precedent: injecting item-appropriate uncertainty improves epistemic control (not route-specific).
limitations: Not read in full in this audit.

authors: Cohen, Roi and Dobler, Konstantin and Biran, Eden and de Melo, Gerard
title: I Don't Know: Explicit Modeling of Uncertainty with an [IDK] Token
claim: Adds an [IDK] token and objective shifting mass to it where predictions would be wrong.
relevance: Same first author as the closest competitor; uncertainty-expression training prior art.

authors: Farquhar, Sebastian and Kossen, Jannik and Kuhn, Lorenz and Gal, Yarin
title: Detecting hallucinations in large language models using semantic entropy
claim: Semantic entropy over sampled answers detects confabulations.
relevance: Sampling-based first-order uncertainty baseline (the 'readout' account).

title: Metacognition and Confidence: A Review and Synthesis
